claims.text: The as-deposited baseline is a non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi high-entropy alloy.
The baseline alloy has a single-phase hexagonal structure.
The baseline alloy exhibits a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
The baseline alloy has considerable magnetocaloric hysteresis.
The controlled intervention is addition of approximately 3–5 at.% Cu.
Cu is a low-cost FCC metal suitable as the proposed additive.
Adding 3–5 at.% Cu will improve microstructural homogeneity in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi.
Cu incorporation will narrow the distribution of local magnetic exchange energies in FeMnNiGeSi.
A narrower distribution of exchange energies will reduce nucleation barriers associated with the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Cu-induced homogenization will reduce transition-associated strain.
Reduced nucleation barriers and strain will broaden the magnetostructural transition.
The Cu-added alloy will have significantly lower hysteresis losses than the Cu-free baseline during low-field cycles.
The Cu-added alloy will exhibit a broader magnetocaloric temperature window.
The Cu-added alloy will retain an appreciable magnetocaloric entropy change, with peak entropy change potentially similar to the baseline.
The predicted changes will improve the alloy's practicality for rapid heat exchange in magnetic refrigeration.
The predictions are expected to apply to the specified non-equiatomic, as-deposited composition under low magnetic fields and without annealing.
Composition changes, different additives, and thermal treatments could alter the predicted behavior.
In the related NiFeCoCrPd HEA system, Pd addition and heat treatment reduced the exchange-energy distribution and increased magnetic or microstructural homogeneity.
The optimal Cu content and magnitude of hysteresis reduction may depend on compositional fluctuations and processing details.
Failure of Cu addition to measurably broaden the transition or significantly reduce hysteresis, or substantial degradation of the magnetocaloric effect, would falsify the hypothesis.
